target.title: feat(modal): support named Secrets
target.body:
## Summary

- add optional Modal environment and named Secret references to trusted user configuration, flags, and environment variables
- resolve Secret names inside Modal without passing Secret values through Crabbox
- derive sandbox environment from the parent App; do not pass Modal's deprecated `environment_name` argument to `Sandbox.create`
- scope inventory to the configured environment
- keep repository-local configuration from selecting environments or Secrets
- document the YAML, CLI, and environment-variable configuration

## Validation

- `go test -race ./internal/providers/modal`
- `go test ./internal/cli`
- `go vet ./...`
- `scripts/check-docs.sh`
- AutoReview: no accepted or actionable findings

## Live Modal proof

Exact-head binary canary against Modal client 1.5.1:

- created a temporary Modal environment and named Secret containing a non-sensitive sentinel
- injected the Secret through Crabbox's generated execution path
- confirmed the sandbox observed the sentinel
- waited for running containers to reach zero
- deleted the Secret and environment
- confirmed no Secret or environment residue remained

No Secret value passed through Crabbox configuration, command arguments, logs, or this pull request.

Exact head: `42c98faa8056fcccf4c5a017426a4e8ed975e091`

target.title: feat: add Herdr plugin
target.body:
## Summary

- add a Herdr plugin manifest with boxes, warmup, prewarm, connect, repository job, and doctor actions
- add a hidden Crabbox adapter that safely consumes Herdr invocation context without requiring jq, Python, or Node at runtime
- add build/path pinning, documentation, packaging tests, and CLI unit tests

## Why

Herdr can install executable workflow plugins directly from GitHub subdirectories. This gives Crabbox users native Herdr actions and managed panes while keeping provider credentials, lease ownership, repository sync, and job behavior inside the Crabbox CLI.

## User impact

After release, users can install the integration with:

```sh
herdr plugin install openclaw/crabbox/plugins/herdr
```

The plugin does not install keybindings or lifecycle hooks. Normal Crabbox job stop policies still apply.

## Publication

No Herdr repository PR is required. Herdr installs manifests from GitHub repository subdirectories, and its marketplace automatically indexes public repositories carrying the `herdr-plugin` topic. After this change and a compatible Crabbox release land on `main`, add that topic to `openclaw/crabbox` so the marketplace advertises a working default-branch install.

## Validation

- `go test ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./internal/cli -run 'TestHerdrPlugin|TestNonBlankLines' -count=1`
- `node --test scripts/herdr-plugin.test.js`
- `scripts/check-docs.sh`
- Herdr 0.7.3 end-to-end smoke: link manifest, create repository workspace, invoke boxes action, verify managed pane changes into the repository cwd, focus pane, and close pane

target.title: docs: add Features capability explorer
target.body:
## Summary

- Reframe the Features index around reusable capabilities rather than providers or command syntax.
- Replace the long generated Markdown list with a polished, responsive capability explorer on `/features/`.
- Add a strong product-oriented hero, a Lease → Sync → Run → Prove flow, live search, category filters, result counts, and linked capability cards.
- Keep provider discovery in the canonical Provider Reference and command syntax in the Command Reference.
- Preserve every existing feature document and URL; the enhancement runs after the normal docs build and only transforms the Features landing page.

## Why

The docs now give Providers a first-class section, but the Features landing page still behaved like a dense Markdown inventory and duplicated adjacent information architecture. It was technically complete but difficult to scan, did not communicate the product workflow, and made dozens of capability guides feel flat and undifferentiated.

This change gives `/features/` one clear job: help a reader understand what Crabbox can do and quickly find the relevant capability contract.

## UX and accessibility

- Responsive three-, two-, and one-column card layouts.
- Searchable capability titles and descriptions.
- Filter pills for each capability area, with pressed state and live result counts.
- Keyboard-friendly native links, buttons, labels, and search input.
- Escape clears an active search.
- Empty-result status is announced and category sections hide only when they have no visible cards.
- Existing light/dark theme variables and reduced-motion behavior remain authoritative.
- Provider and command CTAs create an explicit handoff to the correct top-level section.

## Implementation

The shared Markdown renderer remains unchanged. `scripts/enhance-docs-site.mjs` deterministically post-processes only `dist/docs-site/features/index.html` after the normal build. This isolates the richer landing-page treatment from all other documentation pages and avoids committing generated output.

The Pages workflow and `scripts/check-docs.sh` both run the enhancement, so CI validates the same output that is deployed.

## Visual proof

The `Docs UI Proof / Render visual proof` check builds the exact generated docs output from the PR head, runs the enhancer and regression tests, and renders browser screenshots with pinned Playwright/Chromium.

Its downloadable artifact is named `features-ui-proof-<head-sha>` and contains:

- `features-desktop-light.png` — full desktop layout in light mode.
- `features-desktop-dark.png` — full desktop layout using the dark color scheme.
- `features-mobile.png` — full responsive mobile layout using an iPhone viewport.
- `SHA256SUMS` — digests binding each proof image to the workflow artifact.

The proof job also fails unless the generated page contains the capability explorer, product hero, provider handoff, and command-reference handoff. This makes the evidence reproducible rather than a manually edited screenshot.

## Validation

- `node --check scripts/enhance-docs-site.mjs`
- `node --test scripts/enhance-docs-site.test.mjs`
- Enhancer regression coverage verifies the hero, search/filter surface, capability-card generation, TOC/pager removal, idempotence, and no-op behavior for unrelated pages.
- `Docs UI Proof / Render visual proof` publishes desktop light, desktop dark, and mobile screenshots from the exact built PR output.
- Branch is based directly on upstream `main` (`6da7760693a820c53434b4774077f526d362c136`) with no unrelated files.

Generated site output remains uncommitted.
